caption:
If you automate work in Notion, the billing changed under you. Since May 2026, Notion's custom agents run on metered credits: pooled across the workspace, reset monthly, no rollover. Full Notion AI sits on the paid Business tier.

Metered means an agent that loops spends money while you sleep. So the question stopped being "can I automate this?" and became "is this job worth paying per run?"

Here is the test I use: it has to repeat at least weekly, touch five or more records, and be something you skip when you get busy. One out of three, do it by hand or paste a prompt into a normal chat — that is included and it is fine. The prompt below writes a tight spec with a stop condition, which is the difference between a useful agent and a meter running in the dark.

Save this before you build your next automation. What's the one recurring admin job you'd hand over first?

slides.headline: Spec it before you build it.
slides.sub: Paste into ChatGPT or Claude, then build from the answer.
slides.label: COPY THIS PROMPT
slides.code:
Write a spec for a Notion agent.
Job: [one sentence].
Include: trigger, the exact databases
and fields it may read and write,
stop condition, max items per run,
what to do if a field is missing.
Under 200 words. No open-ended
loops. No steps I cannot check.

body.t: Credits do not roll over, so a big block bought in optimism is money gone.
Start on the smallest amount and check usage after 30 days.
